note: Rewritten from the new-species description in the 1929 paper "New termites from the Antilles and Middle America" held in the library; the original is in English (running head PROC. ENT. SOC. WASH., VOL. 31, NO. 4, APR., 1929). The scan consulted lacks the first page of the paper, so the authors' names are not visible and the citation is given without authors; the type locality is Barro Colorado Island, Panama, and the type specimen is a soldier (USNM Cat. No. 41745). The original describes the soldier only.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It differs from nordenskioldi in the wider head, the shorter pronotum and the deeper, stouter mandibles; from brevipilosus Snyder (Bolivia) in the longer hairs of the head; and from an undescribed species collected by Emerson in British Guiana in the wider head and the longer mandibles. The hairs of the head are longer than in brevipilosus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow, elongate, the posterior margin rounded, the eye spots faintly marked, with many rather long hairs. The opening of the frontal gland is small and lies at the apex of the coronal suture. The postmentum is narrow in the middle. The antennae have 11—12 segments, segment 3 tending to split. The mandibles are reddish brown, long and broad, curved, their tips bent inwards and acute, with 1 tooth near the base. The pronotum is pale yellow with long hairs on the margins, its anterior lobe distinct and very weakly concave in the middle. The abdominal tergites bear long hairs. Measurements: total length of the soldier 4.20—4.60 mm; head with mandibles 2.25—2.35 mm; head to the base of the mandibles 0.80 mm; pronotum length 0.37—0.40 mm; hind tibia length 0.62—0.70 mm; head width 0.95—1.00 mm; pronotum width 0.65 mm.
